reasoning_trace.value: The paper presents an experimental demonstration of the simultaneous transmission of a 60-W power-over-fiber (PoF) signal and a high-speed discrete multitone (DMT) signal over a 1-km 7-core weakly coupled multicore fiber (WC-MCF). The DMT signal is transmitted at 50 GBaud and 60 GBaud, corresponding to data rates of 117 Gbit/s and 140 Gbit/s, respectively. The experimental setup includes a high-power fiber laser, an arbitrary waveform generator, and a photodetector. The results show that the bit error rate (BER) of the DMT signal is below the soft decision forward error correction (SD-FEC) threshold of 2E-2, and the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) meets the 3GPP requirement.

The paper proposes a novel method for high-speed signal light and high-power energy light co-transmission using a 1-km 7-core WC-MCF. The system integrates multiple advanced modulation formats, including DMT, to achieve high-rate and high-power co-transmission. The experimental results demonstrate the successful transmission of 50 GBaud and 60 GBaud DMT signals with a 60-W PoF signal, and the BER performance is below the SD-FEC threshold.

The paper verifies the physical consistency of the reported metrics by measuring the transmission of the 1064 nm PoF signal over 1-3 km of single-mode fiber (SMF). The results show that the collected optical power increases linearly as the high-power fiber laser (HPFL) output power increases, indicating no obvious nonlinear effect of stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) at 1 km. The paper also measures the insertion loss of each channel induced by the fan-in and fan-out (FIFO) device and finds that it is less than 3 dB.

The paper demonstrates the potential of the proposed system for remote application scenarios, such as powering tens or hundreds of low-power consumption devices in the remote unit (RU). The system can provide stable electrical power to low-voltage loads in the Grid scenario, with a temporal fluctuation of the collected power less than 1% over 1 hour. The paper also highlights the importance of the proposed system for future digital grid applications, where high-speed data communication and high-power transmission are required.

key_contribution.gap_addressed: The primary challenges confronting systems capable of simultaneously transmitting optical signals and PoF are twofold: the transmission rate of the signal light is insufficient to meet the high-speed data communication requirements, and the energy-carrying optical power lacks the necessary strength to provide a stable and adequate power supply for the operational load of the RU.
